summary: npm package used as CDN-hosted browser redirect payload
details: The package ships a single browser-side script (px.js) whose only behavior is to inject a full-screen iframe into the host page and navigate it to a hardcoded remote URL (https://mfmz.crcavi.cn/H.html?c=0gjr). There are no npm lifecycle hooks (preinstall/install/postinstall) and the code references `document`, so `npm install` and `require()` in Node do not execute it — installer machines are not directly harmed. The actual delivery vector is jsDelivr (purge.jsdelivr.net/npm/px8my/px.js), which serves the file to any web page that includes it; any site loading the script redirects its viewers to the hardcoded domain. A maintenance shell script in the tarball rewrites the redirect domain, bumps the patch version, runs `npm publish`, and purges the jsDelivr cache — operational tooling for a domain-rotating redirect campaign. The harm targets end-users of any site that embeds this script via CDN, not developers who `npm install` it; route to human review for coordinated takedown of the npm package and jsDelivr cache entry.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
